title: KV ghost-busting and anticipatory decode scheduler for paged-attention
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem statement:
Paged attention workloads exhibit high variance in KV residency: short-lived tokens (chatty UIs) create many small, scattered KV fragments while long-lived contexts pin slots for long durations. This leads to:
- fragmentation that increases memory churn and kernel selection overhead,
- frequent eviction of recently used fragments (thrashing), and
- decode stalling when prefill paths discover missing contiguous KV ranges.

Goals:
1) Reduce end-to-end token latency tail (p95/p99) under mixed short/long context workloads by 15-25%.
2) Reduce unnecessary decode restarts caused by late prefill evictions by 30%.
3) Maintain or improve median throughput for batched requests.
4) Keep changes rollout-safe with feature flags and telemetry gating.

Design overview (high level):
- "Ghost-busting" cleaner: background pass that identifies logically stale KV entries (ghosts) using multi-signal heuristics (last-touch, decode-failure incidence, TTL-probabilistic score) and flags them for low-cost reclamation. Ghosts are not immediately evicted; they are marked with a soft-credit allowing short-lived rehydration without full decode restart.
- Eviction Creditor accounting: instead of immediate eviction, the allocator assigns eviction credits to fragments evicted due to pressure. Credits allow a fragment to be re-inserted in a compacted slot (or prefetched with reduced priority) without counting as a new heavy-prefill. This reduces decode penalty for frequently-reused ephemeral fragments.
- Residency Harmonizer: a background compaction routine that opportunistically coalesces adjacent KV fragments belonging to the same sequence-id into contiguous slots on low GPU load windows. This reduces kernel scatter during attention kernels and improves contiguous memory kernel throughput.
- Anticipatory Decode Scheduler: a new scheduler that starts low-priority speculative decode/prefill for sequences predicted to be requested imminently (based on recent request inter-arrival and route heuristics). It uses a throttled kernel selection path (low-cost kernels and quantized execution) to warm contiguous KV ranges and reduce on-demand decode latency.

Kernel selection implications:
- Prefill warms will preferentially use a compact, lower-precision kernel path to reduce cost (and avoid starving production decode). If the warmed data is later requested in a hot path, a lightweight re-quantize step upgrades the representation.
- Harmonizer outputs metadata for kernel selector (contiguous vs fragmented) to bias toward contiguous-optimized kernels when available.

Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive background compaction improves kernel throughput but increases transient GPU memory copying; we limit compaction to low-util windows and use copy-rate limits.
- Eviction credits can increase residency pressure; credits decay over time and are bounded globally per-tenant.
- Anticipatory decode increases background work; it is gated by per-route allowed speculative budget derived from customer tier and cost-sensitivity labels.

Rollout plan:
1) Feature-flag gated rollout to internal canary tenants (low risk) with telemetry collection.
2) Enable ghost-busting read-only mode (marking ghosts but not reclaiming) for two weeks to validate heuristics.
3) Enable eviction-credit accounting without auto-reinsertion for a small percent of traffic.
4) Turn on limited harmonizer compaction during off-peak hours for 2% of tenants.
5) Gradual ramp once p95/p99 telemetry meets target.

Telemetry & metrics to capture:
- KV fragmentation score (new metric): ratio of average fragment count per sequence to contiguous-run-length.
- p50/p95/p99 token latency before/after speculative prefill hits.
- fraction of decoder restarts due to missing KV ranges.
- speculative prefill CPU/GPU cost and hit-rate.
- eviction-credit utilization and rehydrate hit-rate.

Testing plan:
- Microbench harness: synthetic mixed short/long-context workload with tunable inter-arrival. Regression targets: p99 decode stutter reduced by >=30%.
- Integration: run against staging model matrix (Llama-3-13B, RedGem-7B) and measure kernel selection distribution changes.
- Load test: 72-hour soak with ramped traffic to observe compaction side effects.

Docs & artifacts:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Paged+Residency+Harmonizer+Design
- Perf harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3421
- Initial proto implementation branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/compare/anticipatory-prefill-proto

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Credit decay policy: fixed half-life vs adaptive based on tenant reuse patterns. (Proposal: start with fixed half-life = 10 minutes)
- Harmonizer compaction granularity: page-level vs subpage microfusion. (Start with page-level, expand if ROI high)
- Safe rehydrate path: should rehydrate use the cheaper kernel path always or try to detect downstream hotness and promote?

Acceptance criteria for Done:
- Telemetry demonstrates p99 tail improvement >=15% for canary tenants under mixed workloads.
- No increase in out-of-memory incidents attributable to harmonizer >0.1% over baseline.
- Rollout knobs (flags, budgets) implemented and tested.
comments: 2026-02-21 Maya Chen: Spiked prototype for ghost heuristic. Found that last-touch alone is noisy for chatty workloads. Added decode-failure incidence as an additional signal.

2026-02-25 Diego Alvarez: Implemented soft-credit bookkeeping in allocator. Using per-tenant ring buffer for credit decay. Performance microbench shows 12% p99 improvement on synthetic workload with high ephemeral reuse.
2026-03-01 Review (SRE): Concern raised about harmonizer copies causing allocation pressure during peak. Plan: only run when GPU util < 40% and cap copy bytes/sec. Added to harmonizer throttle.
2026-03-03 Product feedback (Ava Patel): Approve speculative budget model but require opt-out per-tenant. Adding label 'speculative-optout' to tenant metadata.
2026-03-07 Diego Alvarez: Created PR for anticipatory scheduler (https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/3689). Scheduler includes per-route budget enforcement and kernel-path hinting.

2026-03-12 Maya Chen: Canary rollout started on 5 internal tenants. Early telemetry: speculative prefill hit-rate 42%, eviction-credit rehydrate hit-rate 31%. Observed overall p95 down 11% so far; continuing ramp and tuning heuristics.
